mbm-0951.quote: My grandfather’s baduk stones make two different notes against his board. I used to shut my eyes while he set up a problem. I could hear which side was in trouble.

mbm-0952.quote: I built my mecha display on a rainy street made from glossy black paper. One evening my little sister folded a red paper umbrella for the pilot. Now everybody notices the pilot first.

mbm-0953.quote: I sat on the towpath when the freight train crossed the iron bridge. All I could see were wheels and strips of evening sky. That charcoal drawing is the loudest page in my sketchbook.

mbm-0954.quote: I copied my grandmother’s staircase onto a quilt. The third step has an extra strip of batting because it was always the squeaky one. Step on it and I still hear her shushing us.

mbm-0955.clue: How did a feather get into my ballroom shoe?
mbm-0955.quote: My partner’s feather boa caught in my buckle during a turn. We finished the dance with a pink ribbon of feathers between us. I saved the smallest one in the shoe box.

mbm-0956.clue: That button is under civilian protection.
mbm-0956.quote: My pajama top lost a button during the detective show. We spent the ad break looking for it with flashlights. When the detective found his missing diamond, I found my button in the popcorn.

mbm-0957.clue: I can beat the boss with a teaspoon.
mbm-0957.quote: The jump button on my arcade stick stopped working. My dad fitted a tiny spoon handle as a lever. Every time I clear the last platform he asks what’s for dessert.

mbm-0958.clue: I wore the wrong color on purpose.
mbm-0958.quote: I entered the cherry contest in a brand-new white shirt. My aunt marked the first red splash on the pocket with tiny green stitches afterward. It looks like I planned the cherry all along.

mbm-0959.clue: Our timetable lives in the kitchen.
mbm-0959.quote: I draw an engine beside the supper dish each time the local passes while we’re eating. In winter the little trains all line up next to soup. Summer is mostly tomatoes.

mbm-0960.quote: I tied a yellow ribbon to my golf bag to read the breeze. A swallow landed on it before my shot. We all held still until my caddie with feathers flew away.

mbm-0961.clue: Only I know where the green door goes.
mbm-0961.quote: I stitched the houses from the street where we grew up onto a long quilt. Under our own little green door I hid a square of the gingham curtains Mum made for the kitchen.

mbm-0962.clue: My sun chair has a passenger seat.
mbm-0962.quote: I put a folded hand towel beside my deck chair for my neighbor’s old dog. He follows a square of sunlight down the steps. I move the towel when he gives me the look.

mbm-0963.clue: I bought a fan in December.
mbm-0963.quote: The old folding fan at the market had a tiny lighthouse painted on it. I opened it over my desk lamp at home. The lighthouse cast a striped shadow the length of the wall.

mbm-0964.quote: On our beach-cricket wicket one flip-flop kept falling over. A stranger planted a third one behind it as a brace. By the end of the match he was fielding with one bare foot.

mbm-0965.clue: That red square used to go dancing.
mbm-0965.quote: My aunt sent me a torn cuff from her favorite dance dress. I pieced it into the toes of a pair of red quilted slippers. She tapped both feet twice before she’d even tried them on.

mbm-0966.quote: My quilt shows a little fire engine driving along our street. I stitched one side of its ladder loose so my nephew could lift it up. He spends all evening rescuing buttons from the couch.

mbm-0967.clue: My best save kept a king on his throne.
mbm-0967.quote: A friend took a picture of my diving save from right down on the sand. There’s a whole sandcastle in the foreground. In the print I look like I’ve just kept the ball from flattening the king.

mbm-0968.clue: We learned the turn on newspaper.
mbm-0968.quote: My friend and I set sheets of yesterday’s sports section across the dance floor. A scuff meant we’d dragged a foot. Our first clean waltz finished on a photograph of two mud-covered wrestlers.

mbm-0969.clue: I sewed a lamp that turns off.
mbm-0969.quote: My bedtime quilt has a bright yellow lampshade with a flap of navy cloth behind it. My daughter pulls the flap across the light each night and gives the lamp a kiss.

mbm-0970.clue: I know who’s calling from the squeak.
mbm-0970.quote: My radio friend has a swivel chair that squeaks just before he speaks. I heard a bird make the same sound outside and nearly gave it my call sign.

mbm-0971.clue: My sister wanted the other ski.
mbm-0971.quote: After our last lake holiday my sister and I took one old red water ski each. We posed on the dock before we split them. Hers went beside the family photos and mine by the door. Bring our houses together and we could ski again.

mbm-0972.clue: The volleyball has its own passport.
mbm-0972.quote: Every family we played on holiday drew a little picture on one panel. I can spin the ball from a sailboat to a blue bicycle to the bakery that sold us lunch.

mbm-0973.clue: I wait for the last lantern.
mbm-0973.quote: Outside the onsen I sit with my feet in the hot water as the attendant lights the stone lanterns. I watch their orange reflections arrive. By the last one my shoulders have finally fallen away from my ears.

mbm-0974.clue: My camera caught a disappearing act.
mbm-0974.quote: I waited for a street cat to move out of my photo of an empty chair. The shutter clicked just as it leaped. In the print there’s an empty chair and one beautifully sharp tail.

mbm-0975.clue: Look under the wrong cup first.
mbm-0975.quote: I taught Mum my little cup-and-ball trick. She put a sugar cube under the spare cup and fooled me halfway through my own lesson. Tea has become a competitive event at our house.
